sources.title: Rockstar shares 38 new screenshots of Grand Theft Auto 6, showing off Vice City, Jason and Lucia, and much more
sources.text: Rockstar Games have released 38 new screenshots of Grand Theft Auto 6 , ahead of its release later this month. These screenshots, found on a dedicated launch gallery website Rockstar has created , prompts viewers to scroll down and take in the sights of several high quality in-game screenshots snapshotting all kinds of people, places, and events. These include, but are not limited to, a DJ set in-action, a man and his pitbull looking tough to the camera, a tattooed man getting his hair done (machine gun on hand), and a daring motorbike escape. However, my personal favourite has got to be a lively shot of a dive bar. A band - seemingly called The Rusty Anchor is playing - and some older ladies appear to be having a friendly chat with an open-shirt-wearing geezer enjoying a beer. You can find all the new images in an image gallery below. So look through them at your pleasure: Grand Theft Auto 6 is due to release on the 19th November on PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. A few days prior, Rockstar employees are voting on whether or not they'd like to officially recognise a developer union , as the Rockstar vs IWBG union employment tribunal comes to a close on the eve of GTA 6's release date.

sources.title: Every Grand Theft Auto 6 Trailer Released—GTA 6 Gameplay Videos
sources.text: It doesn’t seem real, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming out this month . We’ve been waiting for more than a decade since the last game dropped, and in a couple of weeks (at the time of writing), we’ll have GTA 6 in our hands. Or rather, installed on our consoles, given that it’s not getting a physical disc. If you’re like me, you’re incredibly excited for the imminent release of Grand Theft Auto 6. And if you’re definitely like me, you want to rewatch these trailers over and over again. There’s plenty to go around, after all. Below, I’ve collated all the video content you need to immerse yourself in GTA 6 long before it hits the market. Here’s the full spread of official GTA 6 trailers for your enjoyment. The first Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer shattered viewership records and sent the world into a frenzy at the end of 2023. It was the perfect introduction to the game, but what we didn’t know then was that it would be almost three years before we’d get to play the game. It took a year and a half for Rockstar Games to deliver the second Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer, and when it arrived, it landed around five months before the game was supposed to come out. It would have originally launched in Fall 2025, but it wasn’t to be. This 30-second trailer was enough to whet our appetites a little more, with Rockstar Games finally unveiling the cover art for the most anticipated game ever made. Our deepest look at Grand Theft Auto 6 imaginable came at the end of August, and it introduced a vast, raw cut of gameplay, along with some gussied-up sequences for players to drool over. Just one month before the game was scheduled to hit the market, Rockstar Games revealed the GTA 6 launch trailer. It was only a minute and a half, but it reflected the perfection that was about to arrive… Which GTA 6 trailer is your favorite? Let us know if you’re excited for this game to finally arrive on the Insider Gaming Discord server . For more Insider Gaming coverage, check out our ranking of all the GTA protagonists . And for even more Insider Gaming delivered directly to your inbox, sign up for our newsletter Grant has been gaming for 30+ years and in the industry for 10+. You'll probably find him playing a post-apocalyptic game or an extraction shooter somewhere.

sources.title: Bethesda Is Already Selling The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Merch
sources.text: Hot on the heels of Bethesda Game Studios officially announcing the full name of its highly anticipated next project, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the developer has already put up merch for the upcoming RPG on its online shop. You can be the first person in your friend group with a Sentinel-logo hoodie or T-shirt. And like the Ford Model T, it comes in any color you want, as long as it's black. The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel hoodie is $64.99, while the identical item in T-shirt form is $34.99. Hat tip to @MrMattyPlays on X for first spotting the Sentinel merch. Bethesda says, "Celebrate The Elder Scrolls VI. Your next journey through Tamriel will be in The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Show off your excitement with the official hoodie!" And if you're interesteed in ordering, note the disclaimer: "This hoodie runs small. For the perfect fit, we recommend ordering one size larger than your usual size." The T-shirt shares an identical description, minus the note about it running small. You'll have plenty of time to break in either of these clothing items, as Sentinel isn't expected to be released for at least a couple more years . That would mean it might be at least a decade between the original announcement of The Elder Scrolls 6 and the time it's finally on your hard drive. Regardless, it's arguably the biggest game Xbox has in its portfolio by a country mile and when the release date finally arrives, it's going to be a very, very big deal. Amidst all of the changes at Xbox this year, it will be interesting to see if, a) The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel will be available on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on day one, b) if it might line up with the launch of Xbox's next-gen Project Helix console/gaming PC hybrid , and/or c) if it ends up being an Xbox console exclusive . Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel won't fill the shoes of GTA 6 as the next white whale, says analyst
sources.text: This November has been a terrific month for the number six, with GTA 6 approaching and The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel finally out in the open. Once GTA 6 is in our hands at last, we'll have to reckon with a strange new world where we're no longer constantly waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto – the kind of alien sensation that Hollow Knight: Silksong players, who practically grieved yearning after so much buildup, are intimately familiar with. Will The Elder Scrolls 6 step up to the plate as the next [clears throat] Massive Sequel Over a Decade in the Making That Also Has the Number Six in It ? Is it going to fill Rockstar's enormous shoes as gaming's white whale? "No, I don't think it is," says Circana games analyst Mat Piscatella when I mention this idea in passing. "It's a huge game, obviously, but things like Grand Theft Auto, Call of Duty, NBA 2K, these are games that are huge, mass-market appeal titles." This reflects part of what makes GTA 6 so interesting, not as a game to be played but as an outlier to be observed. Similar to Nintendo, Rockstar can basically do whatever it wants because its loyal audience is big enough. More uniquely, Grand Theft Auto is the type of game that appeals to a huge range of players, from the enthusiasts playing dozens of the best games of 2026 to casual fans who mostly stick to the sports and shooter series that Piscatella mentions. "They're their own thing," he says. "It's a different set of rules, a different set of expectations. They're gonna do their thing, and they've earned every bit of that, just based on what they've done. Nintendo is its own thing, too. They are unique, and I know people hate that and go, 'They're competing just like everyone else.' They are, but with the IP and their history and how they've developed how they go to market, it is a unique proposition. That's why they can do things other companies can't, and they have a relationship with their players that other platforms don't. These are companies or developers that are doing their own thing, blazing their own trail, and a lot of other people try to follow." As AAA game development faces cost crises, Rockstar is making the biggest bet of all, and with the most favorable odds imaginable. Nobody else could make a game like GTA 6. For anyone but Rockstar, it would be too big to succeed. "If you want to talk about a big bet, they don't come any bigger than this, and the appetite for big bets like this doesn't exist in many places," says Piscatella. Even The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, follow-up to one of the most-played RPGs of all time, and handily the most-modded, is in a different weight class. (The Witcher 3 and Skyrim have both sold 65 million copies .) Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more "Whether you're talking about an Elder Scrolls, a Witcher, a God of War, those are big games but they're nowhere near the scale of an NBA 2K, Call of Duty, or Grand Theft Auto," adds Piscatella. "No shade to them. They're all great games and perform very well. But we're talking about a secondary tier to those real mass-market hit drivers." It certainly doesn't help that The Elder Scrolls 6 was announced eight years ago, and re-announced this week with a subtitle, yet we still don't even have a screenshot. The game is reportedly looking at a 2029 launch , which would put it 18 years post-Skyrim, so I'm going to need Bethesda to wake me up for the third time when, and only when, it's got some heat. Bethesda wants you to "show off your excitement" for The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel by spending $35 on a T-shirt Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.title: Skyrim's lead designer has 2 big asks of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, and only one of them is something most players have ever thought about
sources.text: The classic children's board game: horses and ladders. Psst, hey kid, what are the big changes you'd like to see in The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel ? Because all have them, don't we? We've all got our big lists for Todd Howard: Five Easy Ways to Turn This Enormously Profitable Ship Around. You know who else has some changes he'd like to see in Sentinel? Bethesda alum and Skyrim lead designer Bruce Nesmith, who recently sat down with The Examined Game and said that the things he'd really like Bethesda to knuckle down on in TES 6 are mounts and ladders. "I'd like to see a much better implementation of mounts," said Nesmith. "That's been a common complaint; I'm not alone in that." But, at least back when Nesmith was hands-on developing games like this, mounts can be hard to get right. "They're really tricky, there's a lot of hard decisions to be made in those. "You can ride a horse, but that's all you can do in Skyrim. That's it, you just ride the horse. Well, I should be able to do some other things too, maybe fight on the horse, or have it fight with me, you know, stuff like that." In fairness, Skyrim does have some fairly rudimentary mounted combat—though players had to wait for it to be added in a patch back in the day—but I suspect Nesmith would like to see something a bit less awkward in future Elder Scrolls games. I imagine a lot of players would echo Nesmith on mounts. I'm less sure they share his concern about ladders, which strikes me as a very charming and very game-designer-y fixation to have. "You don't climb up and down ladders [in current Elder Scrolls games]. It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders!" But you know what? I'm on board. Not having proper ladders, says Nesmith, "really limits the art team in terms of how they can do multi-layer things. You know, all the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, poof you're at the top, or you have to climb a stair." Advanced ladder tech has its costs, though. "To do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions, which our programmers very legitimately put in front of us, and said 'You gimme answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's gonna take to make them'. And that caused problems, right there". Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. There are, it turns out, a whole lot of ladder questions that arise if you try to implement them in your game. If two people use a ladder at once, what happens? How do NPCs make strategic decisions about them? How do you create animations and behaviours for characters getting hit while climbing, or dying while climbing? All these things and more pile up, which is why Bethesda decided to spend its time on other stuff, historically. Now, of course, it's not Nesmith's problem, and the man wants his mounts and ladders. Bravely, as someone else who also does not have to design The Elder Scrolls 6, I say give them to him. One of Josh's first memories is of playing Quake 2 on the family computer when he was much too young to be doing that, and he's been irreparably game-brained ever since. His writing has been featured in Vice, Fanbyte, and the Financial Times. He'll play pretty much anything, and has written far too much on everything from visual novels to Assassin's Creed. His most profound loves are for CRPGs, immersive sims, and any game whose ambition outstrips its budget. He thinks you're all far too mean about Deus Ex: Invisible War. sources.title: Nintendo Exec Bill Trinen Explains Why the Ocarina of Time Remake Is the Perfect First The Legend of Zelda Game
sources.text: Nintendo of America Vice President of Player & Product Experience Bill Trinen has seen a lot of Zelda games in his nearly 30-year career at the company. He got his start translating bug reports on the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the N64 in the '90s. And with the newly released and critically acclaimed remake, he acknowledged that, internally, there's always a bit of a different buzz when working on a new Zelda game. "Zelda games always come kind of with their own unique energy," he told me at the launch event for the Ocarina of Time Remake at the Nintendo Store in San Francisco. "This moment in particular, I think, is big for all of them [internally], both just because, like, we've talked about how much the game meant to a lot of people back then, but also the role that it plays within the overall Zelda 40th anniversary." The original Legend of Zelda was released for the NES in 1986. Ocarina of Time, in 1998, was the first 3D Zelda game, something that Trinen said this remake release brings back memories of. "The [1998] game itself was just so foundational for [this] kind of 3D adventure game, as a whole, and it just was this moment in time where it was like, everybody was on this journey together." Ocarina of Time has stood the test of time in being regarded as one of the greatest games of all time, but not everyone has played it , whether it was because they didn't have an N64 back then, or that they weren't born yet. Trinen has a message for those players: "This is the perfect place for your first Zelda game, because you are gonna learn everything that there is about the world and the characters that will serve sort of as the foundation for all the others, all the games that came after," he said. "This game is sort of a really foundational story for the lore of the Legend of Zelda. It really tells the story of Link and his journey becoming a hero. It tells the story of Link and his connection to Zelda and their relationship with Ganondorf. And overall, it communicates kind of what is at the moral core of is all the series, which is the idea that wisdom and courage combined can overcome power." Trinen also shared his favorite moment from Ocarina of Time [SPOILER WARNING] . "I have to say my favorite moment in Ocarina is the moment when Link leaves Kokiri Forest for the first time. It's an emotional moment. You say goodbye to a friend. There's a tinge of sadness to it, and then the whole world opens up before you, and you just see Hyrule Fields spread out. And all the possibility and exploration and discovery that awaits, you just sort of see across the field in the list, and you start to wonder, 'Okay, what am I gonna do next?' So it's sort of this really magical moment of almost, you know, leaving your childhood for the first time and setting out into the world, that happens early in the game, and it's a really special part of Link's overall journey." Finally, when I put Trinen on the spot to ask him his favorite Zelda game of all time, he said it's changed over time and answered with a big smile on his face. "Oh, you know, it changes with time. You know, there were points where it was Majora's Mask, and points where it was Wind Waker, or Breath of the Wild. I would say, the role that Ocarina of Time played both in terms of the impact on Nintendo, the impact on the games industry, the impact it had for the series overall, that makes it such a core experience that the Nintendo Switch 2 version is my current new favorite." The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is out now exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2. You can read our review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time Remake Walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas , and Early Item Bag Expansions . sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake reportedly running at 60 fps on PC just hours after game's official Nintendo Switch 2 release
sources.text: Visual and performance issues not quite ironed out yet, which will be music to Nintendo's ears. I've spent all night playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2, and it's a fantastic experience, but some would prefer to tinker and toil over an emulator than enjoy Link's new look. The game is already running on PC, but performance issues are aplenty. You can see progress is moving pretty fast from the emulator crowd, just from these two videos by Unreal Gaming PC on YouTube. Published on the game's official launch day, November 5, this video shows the game getting over the splash screen and running the cutscenes fairly well; however, it suffers from bad flickering, stuttering, and frame rates around the 20-30 fps mark during gameplay. 12 hours later, another video. This time showing the game running between 30–60 fps during gameplay, albeit with some persistent flickering and stutters throughout. There's undoubtedly still a long way to go to a playable experience to match the native Switch 2, but that's marked progress for half a day's work. Especially considering the game is designed for an Arm-powered handheld with very different hardware to what's running the emulator ( Ryzen 7 9800X3D , 64 GB of RAM, and RTX 4080). User akakevinvro on X also posted a video claiming a pretty steady 60 fps. Both are running on the Lichii emulator for the Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2. It's called the "VERY experimental Nintendo Switch 2 emulator" on its GitHub page. It's an open-source project that has similarities to projects of the same ilk, such as Yuzu. Yuzu's developers settled a legal dispute with Nintendo of America and shut down development of the emulator in 2024 . Nintendo has a long history of taking down projects it deems to infringe on its rights, while emulators such as the now defunct suyu often argue that they do not circumvent Nintendo's privacy measures. sources.title: Nintendo says it isn't planning any more Switch 2 price hikes
sources.text: Nintendo, which unveiled the results of the first half of its fiscal year 2027 earlier today , has now said it has access to enough quantities of memory to manufacture more Switch 2 consoles. As a result, the platform holder does not plan to increase the price of the Switch 2. That's according to Reuters , citing Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa. Nintendo, which has so far sold 26m Switch 2 consoles, has already raised the price of the console earlier this year. The price hikes, which took effect on 1st September in the US, Canada, Japan and Europe, saw the console's price increase by $50 / €30 / ¥10,000. Although that was technically the first price hike for the console itself, prior to the Switch 2's launch last year, Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 accessories in the US as a result of the Trump Administration's tariffs. The reason that would cause Nintendo to raise prices again is the same that already caused rival PlayStation and Xbox to do so: AI-driven, global memory and storage shortages . PlayStation already raised PS5 and PS5 Pro prices , on several occasions . Xbox has likewise gone through multiple rounds of price hikes for its Series X and Series S consoles , with the most recent having taken place in August . That same crisis pushed one of Nintendo's longtime ROM suppliers to exit the business , opting instead to focus on the more lucrative business segments. ROM memory is used in Switch cartridges, though Nintendo hasn't commented on the news. Incidentally, Switch 2 hardware sales have been in decline for several quarters now compared to its banner launch in 2025. Still, Switch 2 sales are tracking ahead of the Switch 1.

sources.title: Nintendo says it’s not planning another Switch 2 price hike
sources.text: Nintendo’s president says it will have ‘sufficient’ RAM as shortages drive up console prices.﻿ Nintendo’s president says it will have ‘sufficient’ RAM as shortages drive up console prices.﻿ Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa said during the company’s latest earnings call that it’s “not considering additional changes” to the Switch 2’s price, Reuters reports. The Switch 2 got a $50 price hike earlier this year, bringing its starting price up to $499. Nintendo said in Thursday’s earnings report that Switch 2 sales have dropped 37.4 percent year-over-year. According to Reuters , Furukawa also gave an update on the RAM shortage, saying, “There has been no major change to the memory situation and Nintendo is in a position to secure sufficient quantities.” Earlier this week, one of Nintendo’s Switch 2 cartridge suppliers announced it plans to stop making ROM memory to focus on memory for data centers instead. Demand from AI data centers is driving the ongoing RAM shortages that’s leading to a wave of tech price increases. Microsoft has raised Xbox Series X / S prices multiple times now, increasing the Series S’s starting price from $299 to $499. The PS5 has also been hit with price hikes, taking its starting price up to $649 .

sources.text: Publisher Sony Interactive Entertainment and developer Santa Monica Studio have delayed God of War Laufey from its previously planned February 16, 2027 release date to May 20. Here is the full message from Santa Monica Studio on the delay: Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we’ve been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye’s journey through the Everywhen. We don’t take for granted the trust placed in our studio to make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication of our fans. With this in mind, we’ve made the decision to delay God of War Laufey ‘s release to May 20, 2027. sources.title: God of War Laufey é adiado para maio de 2027; veja a nova data
sources.text: A Santa Monica Studio anunciou nesta quarta-feira (4) o adiamento de God of War Laufey , novo título da franquia protagonizado por Faye, esposa de Kratos. Originalmente previsto para 16 de fevereiro de 2027, o jogo agora será lançado em 20 de maio de 2027 , exclusivamente para PlayStation 5 . A mudança representa um atraso de aproximadamente três meses. Segundo o estúdio, o tempo adicional será utilizado para realizar ajustes finais e aprimorar a experiência antes do lançamento. Em comunicado, a desenvolvedora agradeceu à comunidade pela recepção ao anúncio do jogo, realizado em junho, e afirmou que pretende aproveitar o período extra para alcançar o nível de qualidade esperado pelos fãs. Diferentemente dos títulos principais da franquia, que acompanham a jornada de Kratos, God of War Laufey coloca Faye no centro da história. A aventura acontece após a morte da personagem, quando ela chega a um reino misterioso conhecido como Everywhen . Nesse ambiente, Faye enfrenta criaturas e monstros de diferentes mitologias, acompanhada por aliados incomuns, incluindo um cubo gelatinoso falante e uma faixa de espada que também possui voz. O jogo foi apresentado em junho de 2026 e representa uma nova abordagem para o universo de God of War , explorando uma personagem importante para os acontecimentos da saga nórdica. Até o momento, a Santa Monica Studio não anunciou outras mudanças no projeto além da nova data de lançamento. God of War Laufey chega ao PS5 em 20 de maio de 2027 . O grande destaque é a chegada do Novo Jogo+, um dos recursos mais pedidos pelos fãs de Assassin’s Creed Valhalla . As demais novidades do patch garantem que sua experiência após o fim da campanha e no Novo Jogo+ seja renovada e desafiadora, com recompensas que fazem tudo valer a pena. Confira o que esperar da atualização mais pedida: Conversamos com o designer-chefe de jogo, David Larouche, para saber mais sobre a atualização e como a equipe coloca os jogadores no centro de tudo o que faz. Quais novidades desta atualização são uma resposta direta aos comentários da comunidade? David Larouche : o Novo Jogo+ foi, sem dúvida, o recurso mais pedido pelos fãs. Assassin’s Creed Valhalla é um jogo imenso, mas, para algumas pessoas, jogar uma vez só não basta. Com esta atualização, estamos muito empolgados em permitir que nossos vikings mais dedicados vivam essa aventura novamente, mas, desta vez, com o personagem que tinham ao final da campanha. Como a equipe garantiu que os recursos pedidos atendessem às expectativas dos jogadores? DL : queríamos que a experiência do Novo Jogo+ não fosse apenas jogar tudo de novo; queríamos permitir que os jogadores continuassem aumentando seu poder, percebessem uma progressão em etapas menores e seguissem aprimorando seus personagens. Por todos esses motivos, adicionamos um modo de progressão estendida, mais melhorias para todas as peças de equipamento divino, uma nova categoria de runas e mais de 300 novas opções de bônus de runas que podem ser gravados na Forja de Runas — e todos esses recursos também estão disponíveis fora do Novo Jogo+. Com todas essas novidades, acreditamos que a experiência do Novo Jogo+ incentivará os jogadores a explorar todo o potencial de Eivor. Houve algum desafio inesperado na implementação dessas novidades? DL : acho que o mais surpreendente para nós foi justamente não termos encontrado nenhum grande desafio que nos deixasse sem saber como avançar. Conseguimos reunir uma equipe muito competente de desenvolvedores com experiência em adicionar o Novo Jogo+ a jogos já existentes; o processo de produção foi incrivelmente tranquilo. Há algum recurso que você esteja especialmente empolgado para ver no jogo? DL : com a atualização, transformamos praticamente todos os bônus presentes em itens em runas que podem ser gravadas na Forja de Runas, independentemente de terem sido lançados na experiência estendida, em uma expansão ou até mesmo na Loja. Mal posso esperar para ver como os jogadores vão combinar todos esses bônus e criar os mais variados tipos de sinergia. Tenho certeza de que há muitas combinações poderosíssimas a serem descobertas! Assassin’s Creed Valhalla recebeu sua última atualização de conteúdo há anos. Por que lançar a atualização mais pedida para os jogadores agora? DL : Valhalla pode ter recebido sua última atualização de conteúdo há anos, mas isso não significa que os jogadores deixaram de se importar com o jogo — e nós também não. Sabemos que o Novo Jogo+ é algo que a comunidade deseja há muito tempo e, quando surgiu a oportunidade de finalmente torná-lo realidade, mal podíamos esperar para seguir em frente. No fim das contas, trata-se de dar aos jogadores de longa data mais um motivo para voltar a um mundo ao qual dedicaram tanto tempo e reviver a jornada de Eivor sob uma nova perspectiva, levando consigo boa parte do que conquistaram pelo caminho. O fato de algum tempo ter passado não torna essa experiência menos significativa para nós nem, esperamos, para nossos jogadores. Qual é a importância da comunidade de Assassin’s Creed para a equipe da franquia? DL : a comunidade é extremamente importante para mim e para a equipe. Pessoalmente, acompanho as redes sociais com frequência para ver sobre o que os jogadores estão conversando e, como equipe, prestamos muita atenção aos comentários e às conversas pela internet. Adoramos ver o que os jogadores criam e compartilham sobre nossos jogos. Essa conexão com a comunidade é incrivelmente gratificante e é uma das principais razões pelas quais fazemos o que fazemos. Jogue hoje mesmo Assassin’s Creed Valhalla com a atualização mais pedida no XBOX Series X|S e no XBOX One.

Marvel's Wolverine, as it initially debuted as September's best-selling game, delivering the...

sources.title: Marvel’s Wolverine Has Lost Its Momentum, And Sony’s Numbers Show It

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: PlayStation sees record high player numbers and increased revenue for Q2 2026, and a lot of that success is down to Marvel's Wolverine
sources.text: As part of today's (Thursday 5th November, 2026) financial results, Sony has confirmed that monthly active users, referred to as MAU, across both PlayStation 4 and 5, reached 127 million in September. This represents a seven percent growth year-on-year for the company, and sets a new record high. In Layman's terms, this simply means that more people are engaged with the PlayStation ecosystem now than ever before. And it's not just that there are more people using machines and occasionally booting up their consoles; active play time also increased over the past quarter, too, with total logged play time increasing by four percent, year-on-year. As a result, Sony and PlayStation noted that its Game & Network Services division saw revenue grow by nine percent year-on-year, resulting in operating profit rising by 83 percent year-on-year. Notably, despite its mixed reception , Marvel's Wolverine was name-checked as a driving force for the decent performance over the past quarter - but that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone that's actually been paying attention to how the game performed . The game sold through 2.4 million copies as of 4th November (so, in roughly 50 days). Ghost of Yotei , meanwhile, has sold through 3.3 million since its launch in October 2025. More people playing consoles, and for longer - it must all be good news for Sony right? Well, not all the graphs are showing growth. PS5 hardware sales continue to gradually decline: in the reporting period, Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 consoles, down from 4 million in the same quarter in 2025. But, with 100 million PS5 units out in the wild, and 127 million PlayStation accounts across the whole ecosystem, Sony doesn't seem that worried: instead, the company is now focusing on converting those with active accounts into more viable customers. Elsewhere in the results, we heard from Sony CFO Lin Tao that the PlayStation 6 is on track and "progressing as scheduled" , with "solid progress" expected on the machine in 2027. Regarding those falling PS5 sales, Tao also referenced that, and says it's all part of the natural cycle of console launches and iteration. "Although new PS5 unit sales are gradually declining as expected at this stage of the console life cycle, the PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner," Tao explained. "[Next year,] we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform." It must be encouraging for Sony to see this growth in this quarter, especially after all the bad press and furore around the company's decision to end the manufacturing of PlayStation discs by January 2028 . It seems to be a core part of the gaming audience's understanding of game ownership, the decision has been widely contested as anti-consumer. It's caused a lot of bad blood with PlayStation players over the past six months, but - seemingly, given these results - that has translated to very little material impact on Sony's bottom line.

sources.title: Arkane Union Accuses Microsoft Of “Sabotaging” Development Of Marvel’s Blade

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Arkane union says closing the studio "would probably be more expensive" for Xbox than simply finishing Marvel's Blade
sources.text: "Microsoft based its decision only on stone cold and inhuman logic." Xbox would probably spend more money shutting down Arkane Lyon than it would trying to finish and release Marvel's Blade, according to a union representing workers from the beloved imsim studio. In a statement posted to the STJV (Syndicat des travailleureuses du jeu vidéo) website , the French union claimed that development on Marvel's Blade is "going fine" and is shaping up to be on par with Arkane's widely acclaimed gameography. By choosing to part ways with and potentially close the famed studio, the union says Microsoft is "sabotaging the game it funded." After Xbox's sweeping job cuts and divestments from several first-party studios, Arkane was recently given until December to find a new buyer and ensure its future. Ubisoft Entertainment (Assassin's Creed, Rainbow Six) is reportedly one of the companies interested in buying the studio behind Dishonored , Prey and the upcoming superhero adaptation, though nothing has been finalised yet. The union also blamed many of the studio's problems on Microsoft - a hiring freeze that lasted more than a year supposedly inflated the game's budget and caused additional internal delays. "Microsoft now use those same delay and additional costs as a reason to close the studio," the statement said. "Even this closure itself is done against any financial logic, as closing Arkane today would probably be more expensive than finishing the game," it continued. "The truth is that Microsoft based its decision only on stone cold and inhuman logic, in which our lives, projects and dreams are voided, so we can better serve Microsoft's short term financial goals[...] The decision to close Arkane is solely the brutal application of a never-ending search for maximum profit optimization. Arkane is profitable. Just not profitable for Microsoft." The union's list of demands now asks for employees to be able to have a say in choosing a potential buyer, as well as protections against any layoffs that might happen in the next few years. Should acquisition talks fail, the union claimed that the resources in Microsoft's redundancy package are "outrageously low" - so it's also demanding a redundancy payment of €200,000 per employee and further support. Arkane's not the only developer reeling from Xbox's cuts. Double Fine ( Psychonauts ), Compulsion Games ( South of Midnight ) and Undead Labs ( State of Decay ) all managed to buy their independence, but had to lay off some staff as a result. It's not looking good for Hellblade developer Ninja Theory , either.
